claims.text: Nanoscale chemical heterogeneity creates localized regions with enhanced magnetoelastic or magnetostructural coupling in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Localized magnetoelastic coupling amplifies the magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
Nanoscale chemical heterogeneity can preserve rapid heat exchange while enhancing the low-field magnetocaloric response.
Nanoscale chemical heterogeneity can preserve low magnetic hysteresis while enhancing the low-field magnetocaloric response.
Standard rapid quenching yields a relatively homogeneous microstructure in the proposed alloy.
The rapidly quenched alloy has moderate inherent magnetoelastic coupling.
Changing the processing cooling rate tunes the degree of nanoscale chemical heterogeneity.
Controlled slower cooling produces more nanoscale chemical heterogeneity than rapid quenching.
Localized magnetoelastic coupling promotes cooperative magnetic and lattice responses under low applied fields.
Cooperative magnetic and lattice responses produce a larger magnetic entropy change.
The proposed structural mediation helps maintain low hysteresis.
The proposed structural mediation maintains effective thermal conduction and thereby enables rapid heat exchange.
Slower-cooled samples will exhibit a larger magnetic entropy change than rapidly quenched baseline samples.
Slower-cooled samples will exhibit less magnetic hysteresis than rapidly quenched baseline samples.
Slower-cooled samples will exhibit improved heat exchange relative to rapidly quenched baseline samples.
The rapidly quenched baseline alloy has moderate magnetocaloric properties at low applied fields.
The proposed mechanism applies near Curie temperatures of approximately 230–300 K and at applied fields below 1 T.
The magnitude of the proposed enhancements depends strongly on alloy composition and the extent of heterogeneity.
